tasks.prompt: Order a return sludge control program review at the weekly operations meeting.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant adjusting return control seasonally.
tasks.configuration: Scope: review covering blanket, settleability and return rate data.

cards.label: Assemble blanket depth, settleability and return rate records for the week
Identify periods where blanket depth left the target range
Correlate blanket excursions with return rate and flow at the time
Set the return rate schedule for the coming week, including peak flow settings
Issue the schedule to all shifts and file the review

tasks.explanation: Records are assembled, excursions are identified and correlated with return rate and flow, and the new schedule is issued to every shift.

tasks.prompt: Order the weir and launder cleaning program for a clarifier with algae growth.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional clarifier with algae on the weirs causing uneven effluent flow.
tasks.configuration: Scope: scheduled cleaning of one clarifier launder.

cards.label: Notify the shift team and record the clarifier condition before cleaning
Brush and hose the algae from the weirs and launder surfaces
Check the weir plates are level and firmly seated after cleaning
Confirm effluent flow over the weirs is even around the launder
Record the cleaning in the maintenance log

tasks.explanation: The team is notified and condition recorded first, cleaning follows, weir level and even flow are confirmed, and the work is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order a clarifier stress check ahead of a forecast high flow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant expecting flows well above average the next day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: readiness check the day before a major storm reaches the plant.

cards.label: Review clarifier blanket depths and bring them to the low end of the target range
Confirm all return sludge pumps are available and set to the wet weather schedule
Confirm scrapers, skimmers and drives are running without defects
Check that the standby clarifier is ready to be placed in service if needed
Brief all shifts on the high flow clarifier settings

tasks.explanation: Blankets are lowered first, return capacity and mechanisms are confirmed next, standby capacity is readied, and shifts are briefed last.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a newly cleaned anaerobic digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant returning a mesophilic digester to service.
tasks.configuration: Scope: start up from filling through stable gas production.

cards.label: Fill the digester with warm wastewater or sludge and confirm heating and mixing work
Add seed sludge from a healthy operating digester
Begin feeding at a low volatile solids loading rate
Monitor volatile acids, alkalinity, pH and gas production daily
Increase feeding in steps only after volatile acids stay low and gas production is stable

tasks.explanation: Heating, mixing and seed come before feeding, daily acid and gas checks guard the start up, and loading rises only when the digester is stable.

tasks.prompt: Order a digester feeding rate increase program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional digester running well below its design volatile solids loading.
tasks.configuration: Scope: loading increase over two weeks for a stable digester.

cards.label: Confirm volatile acids, alkalinity ratio, pH and gas production are stable at the current loading
Calculate the new feed volume for the next planned loading step
Increase the daily feed volume to that step
Monitor volatile acids and gas production daily at the new loading
Hold or step back if volatile acids rise, and proceed only when stable again

tasks.explanation: Stability is confirmed before the increase, the new volume is calculated and applied next, and daily monitoring decides whether to hold or proceed.

tasks.prompt: Order the withdrawal and feeding sequence for a digester on a once per day cycle.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional digester fed from a sludge holding tank with a set working level.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one daily cycle that keeps digester level steady.

cards.label: Check the digester level and confirm room is needed for the days feed volume
Withdraw digested sludge equal to the planned feed volume to the withdrawal system
Confirm the withdrawal is complete and valves are returned to normal
Feed the planned volume of raw sludge at the set rate
Record the volumes withdrawn and fed and the final level

tasks.explanation: Room is made by withdrawing first, the withdrawal is confirmed complete, and only then is the equal feed volume added and recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily digester mixing and heating check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional digester with pumped mixing and a hot water heating loop.
tasks.configuration: Scope: morning rounds for one mesophilic digester.

cards.label: Check digester temperature against the mesophilic target range
Confirm the mixing system is running and drawing normal power
Check the heating circulation pump and heat exchanger temperatures
Inspect for foam or level abnormality at the digester sight glass or hatch where safe
Record all readings and report any abnormality to the supervisor

tasks.explanation: Temperature, mixing and heating are checked in order, the digester condition is inspected, and readings are recorded with abnormalities reported.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to rising volatile acids in an anaerobic digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional digester showing souring signs after a loading increase.
tasks.configuration: Scope: recovery program after the volatile acid to alkalinity ratio climbs.

cards.label: Confirm the rise with a repeat volatile acids and alkalinity test
Reduce or stop raw sludge feeding to cut the acid load
Check digester temperature and mixing for a contributing fault
Monitor volatile acids, alkalinity and pH daily while feeding is held
Resume feeding at a reduced rate only after the acid ratio falls back to the normal range

tasks.explanation: The souring is confirmed first, feeding is cut next, temperature and mixing are checked, and feeding resumes at a reduced rate only after recovery.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a digester temperature drop below the mesophilic range.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional digester cooling by several degrees over two days.
tasks.configuration: Scope: response after a heating system fault is suspected.

cards.label: Verify the temperature drop with a second reading or sensor check
Inspect the boiler or heat source and the hot water circulation pump
Check the heat exchanger for fouling or a closed valve
Restore heating and confirm temperature begins rising toward the range
Reduce feeding while temperature is low and monitor gas production daily

tasks.explanation: The drop is verified first, the heat source, circulation and exchanger are checked in order, heating is restored, and feeding is eased while it recovers.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily digester gas system check at awareness level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant gas system checked from outside the digester roof area under the plant safety procedure.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine external check of gas piping, flame arrester and pressure relief devices.

cards.label: Review the gas production and digester pressure trends for abnormal values
Inspect accessible gas piping and condensate traps for leaks, damage or blockage
Confirm the pressure and vacuum relief device appears unobstructed and undamaged
Check the flame arrester and gas meter readings are recorded
Log the check and report any abnormal finding to the supervisor immediately

tasks.explanation: Trends are reviewed first, accessible piping and safety devices are inspected next, and the check is logged with abnormalities reported at once.

tasks.prompt: Order a digester foaming investigation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional digester foaming after a change in sludge feed character.
tasks.configuration: Scope: investigation after foam appears in the gas line and at the digester hatch.

cards.label: Record when the foaming started and what feed or loading changes came before it
Check volatile acids, alkalinity and temperature for digester instability
Review feed sludge for filamentous or industrial contributions
Reduce feeding rate and apply the plant foam control step
Monitor foam, gas production and acids daily until conditions normalise

tasks.explanation: The timeline is recorded first, stability and feed character are checked next, feeding is reduced with foam control, and recovery is monitored daily.

tasks.prompt: Order a digester supernatant withdrawal program that protects the liquid treatment train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional digester with a supernatant layer high in ammonia.
tasks.configuration: Scope: scheduled supernatant return to the plant inlet in small batches.

cards.label: Confirm the supernatant layer depth and sample its ammonia strength
Schedule withdrawals for low load periods at the plant inlet
Withdraw a small batch and confirm the volume sent to the inlet
Watch aeration basin ammonia and dissolved oxygen during the return
Adjust the batch size or timing if the basin shows load stress

tasks.explanation: Strength is sampled first, withdrawals are timed for low load, basin response is watched during return, and batch size is adjusted from that response.

tasks.prompt: Order the preparation steps for taking a digester out of service for cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant preparing a digester for contractor cleaning under Regulation 129/04 licensed supervision.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparation only, ending with the vessel ready for the confined space program.

cards.label: Stop feeding the digester and continue withdrawal until the level is as low as operations allow
Transfer remaining contents to another digester or holding as directed
Isolate and lock out feed, withdrawal, heating, mixing and gas connections
Purge and ventilate the vessel and test the atmosphere under the confined space procedure
Hand the prepared vessel over to the confined space entry team with the test records

tasks.explanation: Feeding stops and contents are removed first, all energy and gas connections are isolated and locked out, the atmosphere is tested, and handover closes the preparation.

tasks.prompt: Order a 30 minute settleability test from sampling to recorded result.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant laboratory running the standard settleometer routine.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one mixed liquor settleability test in a 1 L cylinder.

cards.label: Collect a fresh mixed liquor sample from the aeration basin outlet
Fill the settleometer to the 1000 mL mark and start the timer
Record the settled sludge volume at 30 minutes
Note the supernatant clarity and any rising or floating sludge
Calculate or record the result with the matching mixed liquor solids for the SVI record

tasks.explanation: A fresh sample and a timed test come first, the 30 minute volume and supernatant are observed next, and the result is recorded with its solids value.

tasks.prompt: Order a weekly SVI trending program for the process control meeting.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant tracking sludge quality through the season.
tasks.configuration: Scope: trend review combining settleability and mixed liquor data.

cards.label: Collect the daily settled volume and mixed liquor suspended solids results for the week
Calculate the sludge volume index for each day from settled volume and solids
Plot the SVI trend and mark values outside the plant normal band
Compare the trend with blanket depth and effluent quality for the same days
Present the trend and a recommended wasting or return action at the meeting

tasks.explanation: Daily results are collected and SVI is calculated first, the trend is compared with clarifier performance next, and a recommendation is presented last.

tasks.prompt: Order the quality checks inside a BOD test batch before results are accepted.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory running BOD by the dilution method.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one BOD batch with samples, blanks and a glucose glutamic acid standard.

cards.label: Confirm dilution water quality and seed condition meet the method requirements
Check the glucose glutamic acid standard result is within its acceptance range
Check duplicate sample results agree within the laboratory limit
Check blank depletion is within the method limit
Accept and report sample results only for the checks that pass, and rerun any failed portion

tasks.explanation: Seed and standard performance are checked first, duplicates and blanks follow, and results are accepted or rerun based on those checks.

tasks.prompt: Order a BOD seed check used to decide if seed correction is needed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory using seed from the plant final effluent.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seed evaluation run alongside a sample batch.

cards.label: Prepare a series of seed dilutions in BOD bottles with dilution water
Incubate the bottles at 20 degrees C for 5 days with the sample batch
Measure the dissolved oxygen depletion in each seed bottle
Calculate the seed correction factor from the depletion per mL of seed
Apply the correction to the seeded sample results and record it

tasks.explanation: Seed dilutions are prepared and incubated with the batch, depletion is measured next, and the calculated correction is applied to sample results.

tasks.prompt: Order a nutrient sampling program for one day of ammonia and phosphorus monitoring.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant tracking nutrient removal performance.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sampling at the aeration inlet, basin outlet and final effluent.

cards.label: Prepare labelled bottles and preservatives required for ammonia and phosphorus samples
Collect the influent sample at the set morning time
Collect the aeration basin outlet sample at the matching time
Collect the final effluent sample at the matching time
Deliver all samples to the laboratory with the completed chain of custody form

tasks.explanation: Bottles are prepared first, samples follow the flow path through the plant in order, and delivery with custody documentation closes the program.

tasks.prompt: Order a microscopic sample handling sequence that keeps the organisms representative.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant laboratory examining live mixed liquor.
tasks.configuration: Scope: handling from basin sampling to slide examination within the hour.

cards.label: Collect the mixed liquor sample in a clean wide mouth container
Transport it to the laboratory promptly without aerating or chilling it
Gently invert the container to resuspend the floc evenly
Prepare the slide and examine it while the organisms are still active
Record organism types and activity with the sample time noted

tasks.explanation: Prompt gentle handling protects the live sample, the slide is prepared after even resuspension, and findings are recorded with the sample time.

tasks.prompt: Order a total and volatile suspended solids test sequence for a sludge sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory determining TS and VS for a digester feed sample.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one gravimetric solids determination in the plant laboratory.

cards.label: Filter a measured volume of well mixed sample through a prepared filter
Dry the filter and residue at 103 to 105 degrees C and weigh to get total suspended solids
Ignite the dried residue at 550 degrees C
Cool in a desiccator and weigh again to get the volatile portion
Calculate total and volatile suspended solids and record both results

tasks.explanation: The sample is filtered and dried for total solids first, ignition and reweighing give the volatile portion, and both results are calculated and recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order a 24 hour composite effluent sampling sequence for compliance monitoring.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant sampling under its environmental compliance approval.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one flow proportional composite sample at the final effluent.

cards.label: Program the automatic sampler for flow proportional compositing over 24 hours
Confirm the sampler intake is in the effluent flow and the refrigeration is working
Check the sampler partway through the day for intake blockage or missed pulses
Collect the completed composite, mix it and fill the labelled laboratory bottles
Complete the chain of custody and deliver the samples within the holding time

tasks.explanation: The sampler is programmed and confirmed working first, checked during the day next, and the completed composite is bottled and delivered with custody records.

tasks.prompt: Order the response sequence after a confirmed effluent ammonia result above the compliance limit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant receiving a laboratory confirmed ammonia exceedance for the previous day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: response at an Ontario plant operating under an environmental compliance approval.

cards.label: Confirm the result and check the sample record for sampling or laboratory error
Notify the supervisor and follow the approval reporting duty for the exceedance
Inspect aeration, dissolved oxygen, SRT and alkalinity records for the sample day
Apply the corrective process step for the cause found
Increase effluent ammonia sampling frequency until results return within the limit

tasks.explanation: Confirmation comes first, supervisory notification and reporting follow, process records are inspected and corrected next, and sampling is increased until compliance returns.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to an effluent total suspended solids exceedance from a clarifier upset.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with solids carryover visible at the clarifier weirs.
tasks.configuration: Scope: response over the shift after a high effluent TSS result.

cards.label: Confirm the TSS result and inspect the clarifier surface and blanket depth
Check return sludge rate and flow split between clarifiers
Correct the return rate or flow split found out of position
Resample effluent TSS after the clarifier has stabilised
Report the event and the corrective action to the supervisor for the compliance record

tasks.explanation: The result and clarifier condition are confirmed first, return and split are checked and corrected next, resampling verifies recovery, and reporting closes the event.

tasks.prompt: Order a chlorine disinfection dose adjustment after effluent quality changes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant disinfecting with chlorine and monitoring residual after contact.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dose program change for a chlorinated final effluent.

cards.label: Measure the current effluent chlorine demand indicators, including turbidity and ammonia
Check the current chlorine dose and the residual after the contact time
Adjust the dose by one planned step toward the target residual
Measure the residual again after the new dose has passed through the contact tank
Record the dose change and confirm dechlorination or discharge residual stays within the approval

tasks.explanation: Demand and current residual are measured first, the dose is adjusted in one step, residual is remeasured after contact, and discharge limits are confirmed.

tasks.prompt: Order a UV disinfection performance check for one duty channel.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with a UV channel disinfecting final effluent.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine check of UV intensity, flow and lamp status.

cards.label: Record the channel flow and confirm it is within the validated range for the unit
Check the UV intensity sensor reading against the expected value for the lamp age
Inspect and clean the sensor window and sleeves if fouling is suspected
Confirm lamp status shows all required lamps in service
Record the check and report any low intensity for maintenance follow up

tasks.explanation: Flow is confirmed in range first, intensity and fouling are checked next, lamp status is confirmed, and the check is recorded with follow up reported.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a rising effluent phosphorus trend approaching the limit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with biological phosphorus removal and chemical backup.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisory response over one week of climbing phosphorus results.

cards.label: Confirm the trend from several laboratory results and check sampling consistency
Review biological phosphorus indicators, including anaerobic zone condition and volatile fatty acid supply
Check the chemical feed system is available and the precipitant inventory is adequate
Start or trim chemical feed to hold the trend below the limit
Trend phosphorus daily until the results stabilise in the normal range

tasks.explanation: The trend is confirmed first, biological performance and chemical readiness are reviewed next, chemical feed is applied, and daily trending confirms control.

tasks.prompt: Order the spill and overflow response reporting sequence for a plant bypass event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional event where a bypass occurred and the supervisor must complete the notifications.
tasks.configuration: Scope: response at an Ontario plant after partially treated wastewater bypasses secondary treatment during a storm.

cards.label: Estimate the bypass start time, duration and volume from plant records
Notify the supervisor and the Ontario Spills Action Centre as the approval requires
Collect effluent and receiving water samples as directed for the event
Record the cause, the weather and flow conditions and the actions taken
Complete the written follow up report within the time the approval sets

tasks.explanation: Volume and duration are estimated first, required notifications follow at once, sampling and documentation come next, and the written report closes the sequence.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly effluent compliance reporting workflow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant reporting under its environmental compliance approval.
tasks.configuration: Scope: office workflow preparing one month of results for submission.

cards.label: Collect all laboratory results and flow records for the month
Check the results against the approval limits and flag any exceedance
Calculate the monthly averages and loadings the approval requires
Have the supervisor review and sign the report
Submit the report by the approval deadline and file the copy

tasks.explanation: Records are collected and checked against limits first, required averages are calculated next, supervisory review and signing follow, and submission closes the workflow.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a falling disinfection residual trend at the contact tank outlet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional chlorinated plant with residual trending down over three days.
tasks.configuration: Scope: investigation over one shift before residual reaches the minimum.

cards.label: Verify the residual with a grab test using a freshly calibrated meter
Check chlorine supply level and feed pump operation
Check effluent turbidity and ammonia for a rise in chlorine demand
Adjust the chlorine feed rate for the cause found
Retest residual after one contact time and record the recovery

tasks.explanation: Residual is verified first, supply and feed are checked next, demand causes follow, the feed is adjusted, and recovery is retested and recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order a dissolved oxygen probe calibration and verification routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional probe drifting against handheld readings.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one online probe in an aeration basin.

cards.label: Compare the online reading with a handheld meter reading at the basin
Remove and clean the probe sensor as the manufacturer directs
Calibrate the probe in air saturated water or the standard the manufacturer specifies
Return the probe to the basin and confirm it matches the handheld reading
Record the calibration and the before and after readings in the instrument log

tasks.explanation: Drift is shown by comparison first, cleaning and calibration follow, the probe is verified back in the basin, and the work is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order a pH probe two point calibration routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory with fresh pH 7 and pH 4 buffer solutions.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bench calibration of a process pH probe.

cards.label: Rinse the probe and place it in fresh pH 7 buffer
Set the zero point once the reading is stable
Rinse the probe and place it in fresh pH 4 buffer
Set the slope point once the reading is stable
Verify the probe in a third buffer or sample of known value and record the calibration

tasks.explanation: The neutral buffer sets the zero first, the acid buffer sets the slope second, and a verification check plus recording close the routine.

tasks.prompt: Order a flow meter verification check using a tank drawdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant able to isolate an influent wet well or tank for the test.
tasks.configuration: Scope: verification of the influent flow meter over one timed test.

cards.label: Record the starting level and the meter totaliser reading
Pump or drain a measured volume over a timed interval with the meter recording flow
Record the ending level and the ending totaliser reading
Calculate the volume the meter measured and compare it with the actual volume moved
Record the percent difference and report it if it exceeds the plant tolerance

tasks.explanation: Start readings are taken first, a known volume is moved next, end readings allow the comparison, and the difference is recorded and reported.

tasks.prompt: Order the morning SCADA trend review for process control.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with trends for flow, dissolved oxygen, levels and alarms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisor morning review of the previous 24 hours.

cards.label: Review the influent flow trend for peaks, surges or flat lines
Review dissolved oxygen and blower output trends for control problems
Review tank levels and pump run trends for abnormal cycling
Review the alarm history and confirm each alarm was acknowledged and acted on
Note the days process adjustments in the operations log

tasks.explanation: Flow, aeration, levels and alarms are reviewed in that order, and the days adjustments are noted in the log at the end.

tasks.prompt: Order an ORP trending check for an anoxic zone at awareness level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant using ORP to support, not replace, nitrate sampling.
tasks.configuration: Scope: review of oxidation reduction potential as a supporting indicator only.

cards.label: Confirm the ORP probe is clean and recently verified
Review the ORP trend alongside dissolved oxygen for the anoxic zone
Compare the trend direction with recent nitrate laboratory results
Investigate sampling or probe fouling if ORP and nitrate disagree
Record ORP as a supporting indicator with the laboratory result as the decision basis

tasks.explanation: The probe is verified first, trends are compared with laboratory nitrate next, disagreements are investigated, and laboratory results remain the decision basis.

tasks.prompt: Order an online ammonia analyser check against laboratory results.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional analyser used for aeration control trimming.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly verification of a basin effluent ammonia analyser.

cards.label: Collect a grab sample at the analyser sample point at a recorded time
Analyse the grab sample in the laboratory for ammonia
Compare the laboratory result with the analyser reading at the sample time
Clean the analyser sample line and check its reagents if the difference is large
Record the comparison and arrange calibration if the difference stays outside tolerance

tasks.explanation: The grab sample and laboratory result come first, comparison follows, cleaning and reagent checks come next, and calibration is arranged only if the error persists.

tasks.prompt: Order a chlorine analyser sample line and calibration check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional effluent chlorine analyser with a continuous sample line.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine check after analyser residuals disagree with grab tests.

cards.label: Take a grab sample at the analyser location and test it with a calibrated handheld method
Compare the grab result with the analyser display
Flush and inspect the sample line for blockage or air bubbles
Calibrate or replace reagents as the manufacturer directs if the error remains
Confirm the analyser now matches a second grab test and record the work

tasks.explanation: The grab comparison identifies the error first, the sample line is checked next, calibration follows if needed, and a second grab test confirms the fix.

tasks.prompt: Order the response workflow to a critical high level alarm in a sludge holding tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant where the night operator receives a high level alarm.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm response from SCADA notification to recorded resolution.

cards.label: Acknowledge the alarm and confirm the tank level in the field
Stop or divert the sludge transfer filling the tank
Check the withdrawal pump and downstream path for the reason the tank filled
Restart withdrawal and confirm the level is falling
Record the alarm, the cause and the actions in the operations log

tasks.explanation: The alarm is acknowledged and confirmed in the field first, filling is stopped next, the cause is found, withdrawal restores the level, and the event is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet weather flow equalisation program for a forecast storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant preparing for a major rainfall event.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant with an equalisation tank brought in before peak flow arrives.

cards.label: Review the forecast and the expected peak flow timing
Lower the equalisation tank level in advance to create storage room
Place the equalisation tank in service as influent flow rises
Feed stored flow back to treatment at a controlled rate as the peak passes
Record peak flow, storage used and the return schedule in the event log

tasks.explanation: Forecast review and advance drawdown create room first, storage captures the peak next, controlled return follows, and the event is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order wet weather clarifier protection steps during a peak flow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant at peak wet weather flow with blankets starting to rise.
tasks.configuration: Scope: in event actions for the secondary clarifiers.

cards.label: Confirm all clarifiers in service are sharing flow as evenly as possible
Set return sludge rates to the wet weather schedule
Monitor blanket depths at the set check interval through the peak
Watch effluent solids and adjust return rate if carryover begins
Return clarifier settings to normal once flow and blankets stabilise

tasks.explanation: Flow sharing and wet weather return settings come first, blankets are monitored through the peak, carryover triggers adjustment, and normal settings return after stabilising.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a suspected high strength industrial discharge reaching the plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant receiving an unusual load with falling basin dissolved oxygen.
tasks.configuration: Scope: response after influent appearance and oxygen demand change suddenly.

cards.label: Collect influent samples for BOD, pH and any parameter the discharge approval names
Increase aeration to protect dissolved oxygen as the load reaches the basins
Notify the supervisor and the sewer use contact for source tracing
Divert or equalise part of the flow if storage is available and directed
Monitor effluent quality closely until the load has passed through the plant

tasks.explanation: Samples are taken first, aeration protects the biomass next, escalation and source tracing follow, and effluent is monitored until the load passes.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet weather disinfection capacity check before a high flow period.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant whose disinfection is flow limited at peak events.
tasks.configuration: Scope: readiness check of chlorine contact and UV capacity at peak flow.

cards.label: Calculate the contact time available at the forecast peak flow
Confirm chemical inventory and feed capacity can hold the target residual at that flow
Confirm all UV channels or contact tank cells are in service
Set the peak flow disinfection settings before the event arrives
Verify residuals during the event and record the performance

tasks.explanation: Contact time at peak flow is calculated first, feed capacity and equipment in service are confirmed next, settings are made in advance, and event performance is verified.

tasks.prompt: Order the staffing and supervisory program for a major wet weather event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant expecting a multi day storm.
tasks.configuration: Scope: management program spanning the day before, during and after the event.

cards.label: Review the forecast and schedule added operator coverage for the peak period
Brief all shifts on wet weather settings, sampling duties and reporting duties
Confirm on call maintenance and supervisor contact arrangements
Monitor plant performance and compliance reporting through the event
Hold a post event review and file the event report

tasks.explanation: Coverage is scheduled and shifts briefed before the event, contacts are confirmed next, performance is monitored through it, and a review closes the program.

tasks.prompt: Order the post storm recovery and inspection program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant that ran at peak flow for a full day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: recovery the day after flows return to normal.

cards.label: Inspect screens, grit units and channels for storm debris and flush as needed
Check clarifier blankets, return rates and sludge inventory after the event
Review effluent results from the event for any compliance impact
Return all wet weather settings to normal operation
Complete the event report with peak flow, problems found and actions taken

tasks.explanation: Debris inspection comes first, sludge inventory is checked next, compliance impact is reviewed, settings are normalised, and the event report is completed.

tasks.prompt: Order a load balancing program when influent BOD stays high for several days.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant receiving sustained high organic loading from a seasonal industry.
tasks.configuration: Scope: multi day program protecting the activated sludge process.

cards.label: Confirm the sustained load from influent BOD and flow records
Split flow evenly between parallel treatment trains
Raise dissolved oxygen targets within blower capacity to meet the added demand
Protect solids inventory by holding wasting at or below the normal rate
Review effluent BOD and ammonia daily and ease settings as the load falls

tasks.explanation: The load is confirmed first, flow is balanced and oxygen raised next, inventory is protected, and daily effluent review guides the return to normal.

tasks.prompt: Order nitrification protection during a cold, dilute snowmelt period.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant in spring snowmelt with falling mixed liquor temperature.
tasks.configuration: Scope: protective program while meltwater keeps influent cold and flows high.

cards.label: Confirm influent temperature and flow trends from the plant records
Protect the nitrifier inventory by minimising wasting during the melt
Keep dissolved oxygen at the setpoint despite the dilute load
Watch clarifier blankets closely at the sustained high flow
Resume normal wasting only after temperature and ammonia performance recover

tasks.explanation: Trends trigger protection, wasting is minimised and oxygen held next, blankets are watched at high flow, and normal wasting waits for recovery.

tasks.prompt: Order the morning supervisory process review for an activated sludge plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant starting each day with a structured process review.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daily review by the overall responsible operator style supervisor role under Ontario Regulation 129/04.

cards.label: Review overnight alarms, flows and any compliance sample results
Review aeration, clarifier and solids trends against their targets
Decide the days wasting, return and chemical settings
Communicate the settings to the shift operators and note them in the log
Set the follow up checks that will confirm the settings worked

tasks.explanation: Alarms and results are reviewed first, process trends follow, settings are decided and communicated next, and follow up checks close the review.

tasks.prompt: Order a process adjustment approval workflow for a major setpoint change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant where major changes need documented approval.
tasks.configuration: Scope: change control for moving a plant wide dissolved oxygen strategy.

cards.label: Document the current performance and the reason the change is proposed
Present the proposed setting, the expected benefit and the risk to the supervisor
Obtain supervisor approval and record who approved it and when
Implement the change on one train first as a trial
Review trial results and extend, adjust or reverse the change as directed

tasks.explanation: The case is documented and presented first, approval is recorded next, a single train trial follows, and results decide the wider rollout.

tasks.prompt: Order a shift handover for process control information.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant running continuous shifts with active process adjustments underway.
tasks.configuration: Scope: handover between outgoing and incoming operators.

cards.label: Outgoing operator completes the log with current settings, trends and unfinished tasks
Outgoing and incoming operators walk the key process areas together
Incoming operator confirms the active adjustments, alarms and sampling duties
Both operators sign or initial the handover record

Set the daily wasting volumes for the week
Schedule the midweek trend check that can revise the decision

tasks.prompt: Order the escalation workflow for an abnormal laboratory result.

tasks.prompt: Order a supervised process adjustment carried out by a trainee operator.

tasks.prompt: Order a hypochlorite feed program change for effluent disinfection.

tasks.prompt: Train 2 SVI climbed from 95 to 210 mL/g in ten days while Train 1 on the same influent stayed at 100 mL/g.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Side by side microscopy and DO profile for Train 2 versus Train 1 over a full diurnal cycle

Effluent toxicity test result for the week

clueText.nc-b: Influent nutrients were adequate and identical for both trains, so they do not explain a one train problem.

tasks.prompt: A plant with a long sewer force main developed bulking each late summer, with SVI near 190 mL/g and a rotten egg odour at the aeration inlet.

High RAS rate sheared the floc and produced the poor settling
Chlorine in the RAS oxidized the floc and caused the filaments to grow

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Clarifier sludge blanket depth log for the month
Influent sulfide trend paired with microscopy over warm and cool weeks
RAS pump run time summary

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Blanket depth is a clarifier symptom and does not identify the filament or its food source.
clueText.nc-b: Sulfide and Thiothrix abundance rise and fall together, and both drop when the force main is kept fresher.

A phosphorus deficiency stopped floc formation entirely
Very low F/M and excessive sludge age selected for low food filamentous organisms and poor settling
High influent TSS overloaded the clarifier solids flux

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Influent TSS trend for the month

F/M and SRT trend paired with weekly microscopy filament identification

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

tasks.prompt: Effluent TSS doubled in three days while SVI stayed normal at 105 mL/g and the mixed liquor settled fast in the cylinder.

Old sludge at high SRT broke into pin floc over months
A deflocculating chemical discharge dispersed the floc and caused turbid supernatant despite normal SVI

SVI trend for the previous quarter

tasks.prompt: A viscous, jelly like sludge would not settle or dewater, yet microscopy found almost no filaments.

Dewatering polymer delivery records

tasks.prompt: Settleability appeared to worsen within one shift after the RAS rate was cut sharply to raise the clarifier blanket for a test.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Microscopy filament count archive for the month
Influent flow hydrograph for the week
Blanket depth and RAS rate trend for both clarifiers during the test

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

Primary clarifier sludge draw off log

tasks.prompt: SVI rose to 200 mL/g after the plant switched to a new industrial park connection with high soluble COD and low solids.

tasks.prompt: A sludge settled well in the morning cylinder test but the clarifier effluent was cloudy all day.

MLSS and F/M trend across the storm and recovery period paired with microscopy
Grit removal tonnage record

tasks.prompt: Pin floc appeared in the effluent while the sludge blanket stayed low and SVI was low at 70 mL/g.

evidence.label: Microscopy showed small, dense floc cores with almost no filaments and few rotifers, an old sludge picture.
SRT was calculated at 32 days and wasting had been reduced for two months to build inventory.
Effluent turbidity came from tiny floc particles passing the weir, while the cylinder supernatant held the same fine particles.
A bench trial that wasted a portion of the sample daily produced larger, fresher floc in a week, while the unwasted control kept shedding pin floc.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Filamentous bulking raised the blanket and washed solids over the weir
Low SRT washed out slow growing floc formers
A clarifier scraper fault resuspended settled sludge
Excessive sludge age from under wasting broke floc into pin floc that escapes the clarifier

inference.explanation: SVI and blanket were low, which contradicts bulking and resuspension. SRT was high, not low, and the wasting bench trial isolates sludge age.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Clarifier scraper torque log
SVI and blanket trend
SRT calculation record paired with a wasting trial log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Scraper torque was normal and the blanket stayed low.
clueText.nc-b: Low SVI and low blanket argue against bulking or washout.
clueText.nc-c: Pin floc declines as wasting restores a younger sludge age in the trial.

tasks.prompt: Bulking appeared only in winter, with SVI reaching 180 mL/g at 9 C and returning to 110 mL/g each spring.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Microscopy each winter showed Microthrix parvicella, a filament favoured by low temperature and greasy substrate.
Influent fats and long chain fatty material rose in winter from a seasonal food processor.
DO, nutrients, and F/M stayed in their normal ranges in both seasons.
A bench sample kept at 9 C stayed filamentous, while the paired sample warmed to 18 C lost filament abundance over two weeks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Cold temperature plus greasy substrate selected for Microthrix parvicella and winter filamentous bulking
Winter low DO caused the bulking even though DO stayed in range
Spring wasting changes alone explain the seasonal pattern
Ice in the clarifier mechanically lifted solids each winter

inference.explanation: DO stayed in range, so that distractor is contradicted. No wasting or ice effect is stated, and the paired temperature bench test isolates cold plus substrate.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Seasonal microscopy record paired with influent fats trend and temperature
Wasting log for the year
Clarifier ice observation notes

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Microthrix abundance tracks cold temperature and winter fats, and falls in the warmed bench sample.
clueText.nc-b: Wasting was steady through the year, so it does not track the seasons.
clueText.nc-c: No ice lifting of solids was observed in the clarifier notes.

tasks.prompt: A clarifier passed its morning checks but lost solids every afternoon when a large bakery discharged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Afternoon soluble BOD load doubled for three hours while flow rose only 10 percent.
Oxygen uptake rate in the basin doubled during the discharge and DO sagged to 0.7 mg/L despite blowers at full output.
Afternoon microscopy showed filaments beginning to extend, and SVI rose on high discharge days only.
Equalizing the bakery discharge in a bench simulation held DO above 1.8 mg/L and SVI stayed normal, while the slug fed control bulked.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The clarifier is undersized for the afternoon flow
A recurring soluble load slug caused afternoon DO sag and filament growth, producing the daily solids loss
Afternoon heat caused thermal short circuiting in the clarifier
The bakery discharge contained a biocide that killed the floc

inference.explanation: Flow rose only slightly, so hydraulic undersizing does not fit. No thermal pattern or cell death is stated, floc stayed active with a doubled uptake rate, and the equalization simulation isolates the load slug.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Clarifier dye test record
Bakery discharge schedule paired with basin DO and uptake rate trend
Effluent toxicity screening result

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: The dye test showed normal flow distribution.
clueText.nc-b: DO sag and SVI rise follow the discharge window and disappear under equalized feeding.
clueText.nc-c: Toxicity screening was negative and uptake rate doubled, showing live, hungry biomass.

tasks.prompt: A thick, dark brown, greasy foam covered the aeration basin and the clarifier surface for six weeks.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Microscopy of the foam showed Nocardia type branching filaments concentrated in the foam, far more than in the mixed liquor.
SRT was 18 days and the plant received greasy influent from a large food court complex.
Foam trapped solids, and clarifier effluent TSS rose when wind blew foam over the weir.
Skimming foam to waste in a trial bay reduced foam solids inventory week by week, while the unskimmed paired bay kept its foam layer.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Ordinary aeration foam from young sludge is covering the basin
Denitrification gas is floating the foam layer in the basin
Nocardia type foam formers, favoured by long SRT and greasy substrate, built a stable foam that must be wasted from the surface
A detergent spill created a white surfactant foam

inference.explanation: Young sludge foam is light and short lived, denitrification acts in clarifiers, and detergent foam is white and soapy. Branching filaments concentrated in dark greasy foam, long SRT, and the skimming trial identify Nocardia.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Influent detergent complaint log
Clarifier gas bubble observations
Foam microscopy record paired with an SRT and foam wasting trial log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: No detergent spill was logged and the foam is dark and greasy, not white.
clueText.nc-b: Basin foam is present before the clarifier, so clarifier gas cannot explain it.
clueText.nc-c: Foam filament counts fall only in the bay where foam is skimmed to waste.

tasks.prompt: White, billowy foam piled on the basin the week after the plant reseeded following a shutdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: MLSS was only 700 mg/L and F/M was 0.9 kg BOD per kg MLVSS per day in the first week after reseeding.
Microscopy showed small floc, many free bacteria, and no foam forming filaments in the foam itself.
Foam was light, white, and collapsed quickly when sprayed with water in a bench tray test.
As MLSS built past 1800 mg/L over two weeks, the foam faded without any foam control chemical.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Nocardia foam established itself in the first week
Microthrix foam from cold greasy influent caused the white foam
Excess antifoam chemical from storage caused the foam
Young sludge at high F/M after reseeding produced temporary start up foam

inference.explanation: The foam held no filaments, collapsed with water spray, and faded as biomass built, which contradicts established filamentous foam. No antifoam addition is stated.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Foam microscopy and bench collapse test record from the reseeding week
Influent grease trend for the month
Antifoam chemical inventory log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Foam with no filaments that collapses in water and fades as MLSS rises confirms start up foam.
clueText.nc-b: Grease was normal and the foam contained no Microthrix.
clueText.nc-c: Antifoam inventory showed no use during the reseeding week.

tasks.prompt: Foam returned within days every time wasting was increased to control it, and MLSS kept falling.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The foam layer held an estimated 30 percent of the system solids inventory by a foam solids survey.
Microscopy showed foam former filaments dominant in the foam and scarce in the mixed liquor below.
Wasting from the mixed liquor lowered SRT for the bulk sludge but the foam layer itself was never removed.
A trial wasting foam directly off the surface cut foam coverage in ten days, while mixed liquor wasting alone in the paired basin did not.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Wasting mixed liquor cannot control foam formers that live in the foam layer, so foam itself must be wasted
The foam returns because wasting was too slow and more mixed liquor wasting is the answer
Foam returns because RAS chlorination was stopped
Foam returns because influent grease doubled in the same period

inference.explanation: The paired trial directly contradicts the more wasting distractor, grease did not change in the record, and no chlorination change is stated. The solids survey shows where the inventory sits.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Influent grease analysis for the period
Foam solids survey paired with the surface wasting trial log
RAS chlorination dose log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Grease was steady during the trial period.
clueText.nc-b: Foam coverage falls only where foam itself is removed to waste.
clueText.nc-c: Chlorination dose was unchanged through the trial.

tasks.prompt: A stable scum blanket formed on the secondary clarifier but the aeration basin surface stayed clear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Clarifier scum contained gas bubbles and rose from the blanket, and it thickened when RAS was slowed for a weekend test.
Nitrate in the clarifier feed was 14 mg/L and the blanket was warm at 21 C.
Microscopy of the scum showed ordinary floc with no foam former filaments.
Increasing RAS withdrawal during a trial weekend kept the blanket thin and the scum did not form, while nitrate stayed the same.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Nocardia foam migrated from the basin to the clarifier
Denitrification in a deep, slow moving clarifier blanket floated solids as scum, not filamentous foaming
Grease from the influent floated as a scum layer
Algae grew on the clarifier surface and formed the blanket

inference.explanation: The basin was clear and the scum held ordinary floc with bubbles, which contradicts foam formers and grease. The RAS trial isolates blanket residence time and denitrification gas.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Basin foam microscopy record
Influent grease trend
Clarifier blanket residence check paired with nitrate and RAS trial log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Basin microscopy showed no foam formers to migrate.
clueText.nc-b: Grease was normal and the scum was floc with gas bubbles, not grease.
clueText.nc-c: Scum forms only when the blanket sits, and disappears when the blanket is kept moving.

tasks.prompt: Foaming worsened after operators raised MLSS to prepare for a winter load increase.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: SRT rose from 11 to 21 days as MLSS was built up, and foam coverage grew in step with SRT.
Microscopy showed Microthrix and Nocardia type filaments, both favoured by long sludge age.
Grease in the influent was unchanged from the previous season.
A trial bay held at the lower SRT kept a thin foam layer, while the high SRT bay foamed heavily on the same influent.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The winter load increase itself foamed the basin
Cold air from the blowers chilled the mixed liquor and caused foam
Raising SRT to build MLSS also selected for long age foam formers and caused the foaming
New diffusers installed that month whipped the surface into foam

inference.explanation: Grease and load were steady, and the paired SRT trial isolates sludge age. No diffuser or chilling effect is stated, and foam formers are documented in the foam.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Paired bay SRT and foam coverage log with foam microscopy
Blower intake temperature log
Diffuser installation record

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Foam tracks SRT between the paired bays on identical influent.
clueText.nc-b: Blower air temperature does not select for foam forming filaments.
clueText.nc-c: Diffusers were not changed in the high foam bay during the trial.
